To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the macroscopic gravity approach to backreaction is fully covariant, 2) the backreaction remains small well into the matter domination era, 3) the backreaction can be calculated in any situation (even nonlinear) where the metric is in the perturbed FLRW form.

(i) we have developed a fully covariant formalism for the study of cosmological perturbation in macroscopic gravity; (ii) we have derived the backreaction in this framework, and (iii) we have shown that the backreaction is negligible well into the non-linear regime.

the backreaction of cosmological perturbation can be calculated in the framework of macroscopic gravity, that it can be calculated for any situation where the metric can brought to perturbed Friedmann-Robertson-Lemaitre-Walker form, that the backreaction can be calculated without the use of gauge fixing conditions, and that the backreaction in the case of linear perturbations around a homogeneous and isotropic universe remains negligible well into matter domination.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of corrections to the Einstein equations due to inhomogeneities in the cosmological setting.
the backreaction of inhomogeneites in cosmology in the context of Zalaletdino's macroscopic gravity.
the problem of backreaction of cosmological pertubations in covariant macroscopic (Zalaletdinov) gravity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the backreaction is small in the matter-dominated era and that the linear perturbation theory can be trusted in this regime.
the backreaction is negligible for any realistic cosmological model.
the problem of backreaction in cosmology has not been solved.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the problem of backreaction in macroscopic gravity is well posed, and the results of our calculations are encouraging for future investigations.
, while the backreaction is small in the linear regime, the question of its relevance in the nonlinear regime remains open.
, in contrast to the situation in standard cosmology, the backreaction does not lead to a breakdown of the Friedmann equations, and therefore does not pose a problem for macroscopic gravity.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, at least in the linear regime and in the context of macroscopic gravity, there is no reason to believe that the backreaction of cosmological perturbation is large enough to significantly affect cosmological evolution.
, at least in the linear perturbation regime considered here, the problem of backreaction does not lead to any serious issues.

, in the context of cosmological perturbation, the framework of macroscopic gravity can be adapted to a form which is free from the gauge related ambiguities which plague other approaches to the problem of backreaction.
